name: Nearchus sails from the Indus
summary: Nearchus leads Alexander's fleet from the Indus along the Makran coast, through the Strait of Hormuz and around the Persian side of the Gulf. Local pilots help the ships find their way between difficult supply stops. After reaching Diridotis, the fleet turns back and ascends the Pasitigris to rejoin the army. Arrian's Indica preserves an account based on Nearchus's lost narrative; ancient harbours and river mouths are mapped approximately.

stops.note: The fleet prepares in the Indus delta before descending towards the sea.
A short halt at a sandy island after leaving the Indus; the longer windbound stay comes at the next harbour.
At a sheltered harbour, often placed near present-day Karachi, the fleet waits 33 days for the sea winds to ease.
Leonnatus supplies ten days of grain; damaged ships are repaired and crews reorganised.
At the river usually identified with the Hingol, the fleet forces a landing against local resistance.
Rounding the headland marks the passage from the Oritan coast towards Gedrosia.
The local pilot Hydraces joins the fleet and guides it towards Carmania; the harbour's exact site is uncertain.
Water and grain are difficult to obtain along Makran. Arrian describes fishing communities and an encounter with whales.
Cultivated land appears on the Carmanian coast. The fleet turns north-west towards the Strait of Hormuz.
The fleet refits by the Anamis, near the Minab river. Nearchus goes inland to meet Alexander, then returns to command.
At the island usually identified with Qeshm, the local ruler Mazenes volunteers to pilot the remaining voyage.
Following the Persian side of the Gulf, the fleet calls at islands where Nearchus records pearl fishing.
A narrow river entrance and falling tide make the anchorage difficult on the Persian coast.
The fleet passes a peninsula with gardens and fruit trees near the area of modern Bushehr.
Beyond the Arosis, shallow muddy channels require the ships to follow navigation stakes in single file.
At a trading port near the ancient Euphrates outlet, news of Alexander sends the fleet back east; the site's position is approximate.
The fleet retraces its course across the estuary and enters the Pasitigris, the Karun river system.
The fleet meets Alexander at his river crossing on the way to Susa. The reunited forces celebrate, and Nearchus receives a gold crown.

informs.note: Nearchus's coastal voyage, preserved in Arrian's Indica
